en: Krishna said: They speak of an undying fig tree with its roots above and its branches below. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns. Whoever knows this tree knows the Vedas.
Its branches spread below and above, fed by the gunas, with sense objects as their buds. Below, in the human world, its roots stretch on, binding people to action.
Its real form is not seen here, nor its end, its beginning or its base. Cutting down this firmly rooted fig tree with the strong axe of non-attachment,
one should then seek that place from which those who reach it never return, thinking: 'I take refuge in that first Person from whom this ancient flow of the world came forth.'

Free from pride and confusion, having overcome the fault of attachment, always turned toward the Self, with desires gone, freed from the pairs called pleasure and pain, the clear-minded reach that undying place.

first: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
en: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire lights that place. Those who go there do not return. That is my highest home.
A part of me, eternal, has become the living soul in the world of the living. It draws to itself the five senses and the mind, which rest in nature.
When the soul, as master, takes a body and when it leaves one, it carries these along, as the wind carries scents from their source.

first: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
en: Using the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, and the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.

first: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
en: The confused do not see it when it leaves the body, stays in it, or enjoys things through the gunas. Those with the eye of knowledge see it.
Yogis who strive see it living in themselves. But those whose minds are not made pure and who lack awareness do not see it, even if they strive.
The light in the sun that brightens the whole world, the light in the moon and in fire: know that light to be mine.
Entering the earth, I hold up all beings with my strength. Becoming the juicy moon (soma), I feed all plants.
Becoming the digestive fire in the bodies of living beings and joined with the in-breath and out-breath, I digest the four kinds of food.
I live in the heart of everyone. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am what is to be known through all the Vedas; I am the maker of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.

first: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।
en: There are two persons in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are the perishable; the unchanging one is called the imperishable.
But there is another, the highest Person, called the supreme Self, the undying Lord who enters the three worlds and holds them up.
Because I am beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as the Highest Person.
Whoever, free from confusion, knows me in this way as the Highest Person knows everything and worships me with their whole being, Bharata.
So I have given you this most secret teaching, sinless one. Understanding it, a person becomes wise and has done all that needs to be done, Bharata.
